title: Derive evidence review status summary from existing review state
decision: Add the status summary inside the existing client-side evidence review workflow by deriving counts from `seededEvidenceReview.criteria`, `criterionStates`, and the current selected evidence state. Keep the summary as presentational UI in `app/evidence-review-workflow.tsx` and avoid new persistence, API routes, or duplicated verdict state.
evidence: `prd.json` requests a compact status summary that updates when a criterion verdict or selected evidence changes.
`app/evidence-review-workflow.tsx` already owns `criterionStates` with React state and recalculates `verdict` from those states.
`lib/evidence-review.ts` already defines required criteria, criterion verdict states, selected evidence IDs, and `calculateReviewVerdict`.
`target-docs/INDEX.md` lists source roots as `app` and `lib`, integrations as none discovered, and persistence/auth as unknown.
`BUILD_GUIDE.md` says to preserve existing files and use the current Next.js app roots.
impact: The summary will update naturally through React state changes without a second source of truth.
Implementation remains local to the existing workflow component unless tests need helper extraction.
Tests can assert the visible counts and state JSON through existing component/browser coverage.

title: Render blocker callout from existing verdict reasons
decision: Add the blocker callout next to the current final verdict UI and drive its content from the existing `verdict.status` and `verdict.reasons`. When the status is blocked or rejected, list the concrete reasons. When accepted, render a stable accepted-state message from the accepted verdict reason.
evidence: `prd.json` requests visible blocked/rejected reasons in a stable, testable callout and an accepted-state message after all required review criteria pass with selected evidence.
`app/evidence-review-workflow.tsx` already renders a `final-verdict` section from the same verdict object.
`target-docs/INDEX.md` says to preserve current architecture unless the PRD requires change.
impact: No new verdict computation is needed for the callout.
The callout can use stable `data-testid` attributes for browser and unit-level assertions.
Accepted, blocked, and rejected states stay aligned with existing domain logic.

title: Build summary before blocker callout
decision: Implement `evidence-review-status-summary` first, then `evidence-review-blocker-callout`, because the PRD declares the callout dependent on the summary and both features share the same visible review state.
evidence: `build-spec.md` already lists both features in that order.
The current workflow state in `app/evidence-review-workflow.tsx` supports both features from the same `criterionStates` and `verdict` values.
impact: The build can add shared derived review status data once and use it for both UI additions.
Verification should cover the initial blocked state, a changed criterion state, and the accepted state after all required criteria pass with evidence.
The implementation remains compatible with the existing `make check`, `make test`, `make build`, and `make test-e2e` targets.
